observations.text: SP, due to an unrehearsed route frequency plan, did not establish two-way communication with the radar control station before entering its control area, with the result that the IP selected the frequency and passed the initial contact call. The remaining en route calls were made only as directed by the IP. Study of the standard radio procedures and of the frequency sequence of the route is required.

SP, due to distraction from the primary scan by an unrelated switch action, did not continuously monitor the assigned frequency and missed two calls addressed to the aircraft, with the result that the IP answered the ground station and took over the R/T for the remainder of the leg. Radio procedures were not executed without support from the IP.

SP obtained contact with the ground stations following the standard phraseology and complied with the instructions received, completing the R/T sequence of the route after the IP's verbal prompts at two frequency changes. Recognition of the required initial contact came with delay at the second radar control area boundary. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a self-initiated frequency change with unprompted initial contact is expected in the next sortie.

SP monitored the assigned frequencies continuously and responded to all calls without delay, obtaining contact with each radar control station before entering its control area on his/her own initiative. Two minor phraseology errors on the initial contact calls were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed all R/T procedures of the route accurately and without any support from the IP, obtaining positive contact with every radar control station before entering its control area and using the brevity words correctly. Instructions given by the ground stations were read back and followed precisely, without misinterpretations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP managed the R/T of the entire route to a standard well above that expected at this stage, with standard phraseology, immediate responses and correct use of brevity words on every transmission. Initial contact was established with all radar control stations ahead of their control area boundaries and no transmission interrupted communication in progress between the ground station and other aircraft. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to incorrect handling of the frequency changes required by the route, did not establish two-way communication with the second radar control station and transmitted on the previous frequency, with the result that the IP had to reset the R/T and execute the initial contact. The position reports for the remaining turning points were passed by the IP. Further study of the radio procedures and of the route frequency plan is required.

SP, due to an unstated request for a repeat of the instruction that was not understood, accepted a re-routing from the radar control station without clarification and did not follow the instruction given, with the result that the IP intervened, transmitted the correction and directed the subsequent R/T. Instructions were not followed precisely and without misinterpretations.

SP, due to a non-standardized R/T flow at the frequency changes, did not execute the initial contact with the radar control station before entering its control area, with the result that the required call was made only after the IP's verbal prompt. The omission was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to non-standard phraseology that left the intention ambiguous to the controller, did not obtain contact following the standard procedures and phraseology, with the result that two transmissions had to be repeated at the station's request and the correct wording was used only after the IP's verbal prompts. The errors were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP performed the R/T of the route within the desired standards, establishing two-way communication with all stations and following the instructions received without misinterpretations. The responses to two calls from the radar control station were delayed while attention was on map reading, and both were corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - continuous monitoring of the assigned frequency during the navigation tasks is expected to improve.

SP executed all radio procedures without any support from the IP, obtaining positive contact with each radar control station before entering its control area and using brevity words where required. The responses to the ground stations were immediate and every instruction was read back and complied with precisely. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP handled the R/T of the entire navigation route with exceptional accuracy, with standard phraseology on every transmission, immediate responses and correct use of brevity words during the busy segments. Frequency changes and initial contacts were anticipated and executed ahead of each control area boundary, and no transmission interrupted communication in progress between the ground station and other aircraft. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the R/T procedures required for the route, did not establish two-way communication with the radar control station and could not complete the position report without assistance, with the result that the IP executed the initial contact and passed the report. The remaining route calls were directed by the IP. Review of the standard radio procedures and of the route frequency plan is required.

SP, due to a technically worded transmission where plain language was required to convey the situation, did not make the aircraft's actual condition understood by the ground station after the deviation from the planned track, with the result that the IP took over the R/T and restated the request. Contact with the control station was not obtained following the standard procedures and phraseology.

SP, due to late reference to the frequency plan at the turning points, did not execute the initial contact with the radar control station before entering its control area, with the result that positive contact was obtained only after the IP's verbal prompt. The omission was recognized and corrected with delay, and the same prompt was required at the following frequency change.

SP, due to failure to pass a required call at the briefed point, did not report the position over the second turning point to the radar control station, with the result that the report was transmitted only after the IP's verbal indication. The requirement was recognized with delay and a further prompt was needed for the arrival call.

SP, due to an incomplete read-back technique, did not repeat the assigned altitude of the clearance received from the radar control station, with the result of a minor procedural error, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. All remaining instructions were followed precisely and the route frequency changes were executed on his/her own initiative.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task at the turning point, did not respond as soon as possible to a call from the radar control station and transmitted while the station was working another aircraft, with the result of two minor communication errors, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Standard phraseology was maintained for the remainder of the route.

SP executed the radio procedures of the route within the desired standards, obtaining positive contact with every radar control station before entering its control area and following all instructions without misinterpretations. Phraseology was standard, although the initial contact call at the second control area boundary was passed later than the briefed point and the brevity words were used only after the IP's example. Marginal performance for the Training Section - anticipation of the frequency changes and consistent use of brevity words are expected to improve.

SP managed the R/T of the entire navigation mission with exceptional accuracy and speed, using standard phraseology and correct brevity words on every transmission, without any support from the IP. Positive contact was established with each radar control station well ahead of its control area boundary, all instructions were read back and complied with precisely, and no transmission interrupted communication in progress between the ground station and other aircraft. Above end of block MIF achieved.
